extracted.intended_audience: individual writers (academic and non-academic) applying for the NEH Public Scholars grant
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for preparing and submitting an application to the National Endowment for the Humanities Public Scholars program, which funds well‑researched nonfiction books for a broad public. Covers eligibility, required materials, submission steps, and program priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program purpose / target project
rubrics_metrics.description: The Public Scholars program supports the creation of well-researched nonfiction books in the humanities written for the broad public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It does so by offering grants to individual authors for research, writing, travel, and other activities leading to publication. The program is intended both to encourage non-academic writers to deepen their engagement with the humanities by strengthening the research underlying their books and to encourage academic writers in the humanities to communicate the significance of their research to the broadest possible range of readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible applicants (open to)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Writers with or without an academic affiliation may apply, and no advanced degree is required. NEH especially encourages applications to this program from independent writers, researchers, scholars, and journalists. The program continues to offer special encouragement to independent writers who do not have a long-term position at an academic institution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expected output
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The grant is intended to support activities that lead to publication of a well-researched nonfiction book for a broad public audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maximum award amount
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use of funds is to support research, writing, travel, and other activities leading to publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Period of performance
rubrics_metrics.description: Period of performance: Six to twelve months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must plan project activities to fit within a six- to twelve-month funded period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrative page limit
rubrics_metrics.description: The page limit for the narrative section of the application has been reduced from four pages to three pages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must confine the application narrative to three pages; follow the Notice of Funding Opportunity and application instructions for formatting and content expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required one-page plan of work attachment
rubrics_metrics.description: A new required one-page attachment indicating your plan of work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This one-page plan is mandatory and should concisely describe how you will carry out the project within the period of performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required form indicating locations of work
rubrics_metrics.description: A new required form indicating the location(s) where you will carry out your plan of work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You must provide the form specifying the physical locations where project activities will be conducted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Read the Notice of Funding Opportunity
rubrics_metrics.description: Read the Notice of Funding Opportunity to ensure you understand all the expectations and restrictions for projects delivered under this program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice contains essential details about eligibility, allowable costs, application components, and restrictions; applicants should follow it closely to write the most effective application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application submission via Grants.gov (registration)
rubrics_metrics.description: Register for an account on Grants.gov.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As soon as you know you're ready to apply, make sure you register for a Grants.gov account as this is vital to the application process. If you already have registered, make sure it is up to date. (Links provided: Register for Grants.gov: Individuals; Grants.gov Self Service Knowledge Base; Grants.gov Applicant Tools and Tips.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Prepare PDFs and application package
rubrics_metrics.description: Follow the instructions outlined in the Notice of Funding Opportunity and Grants.gov instructions to complete your application package.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Download Adobe Reader and follow tips for making PDFs. Use the Public Scholars Grants.gov application package and included program resources and sample narratives as models.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submit and verify Grants.gov confirmations
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit your application package on Grants.gov; you will receive a confirmation from Grants.gov when you've successfully submitted your application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grants.gov will send up to five e-mail messages confirming receipt of your application at different stages in acceptance. You should verify that you have received all confirmation messages. Note that email filters may send these messages to spam or junk folders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitor status of letters of recommendation
rubrics_metrics.description: NEH requests letters of reference from your recommenders approximately seven to ten days after the application deadline. You will be notified by e-mail when each of your letters of reference has been received.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After receiving the fifth Grants.gov confirmation message (confirming NEH received your application), you may check the status of your letters by logging in to the secure area of NEH’s website using your NEH application number and Grants.gov tracking number. You will see names and e-mail addresses of letter writers and whether their letters have arrived. If necessary, you may send reminders to your letter writers (including the upload link) from this site. You are responsible for ensuring that your letter writers have received the solicitations from NEH and submitted their letters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of grant funds / allowable activities
rubrics_metrics.description: The program offers grants to individual authors for research, writing, travel, and other activities leading to publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Budget your proposal around these allowable activities and describe how funds will support completion of the book project within the funded period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program timeline and deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: The Notice of Funding Opportunity announces two deadlines (in December 2020 and December 2021); application available December 23, 2020; application due December 15, 2021; expected notification date August 12, 2022; project start dates September 1, 2022 and September 1, 2023.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adhere to the announced deadlines and planned project start dates; consult the specific Notice for the cycle you are applying to for exact dates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Samples and examples to model expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Program Resources include Sample Application Narratives and a List of recently funded Public Scholar projects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review sample narratives (listed examples include a range of topics) and recently funded projects to understand the kinds of projects and application quality the program funds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessibility contact information
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants who are deaf or hard of hearing can contact NEH via Federal Relay (TTY users) at 800-877-8399.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the provided contact information for accessibility-related questions or assistance.
